tasks.title: Implement Phase Management System
tasks.description: Create a centralized phase state management system with possible values: combat, shop, death, lab. Implement automatic phase transitions based on game state.
tasks.details: Create a React context provider for phase management with state: type Phase = 'combat' | 'shop' | 'death' | 'lab'. Implement transition logic: Combat → Shop (when all enemies dead), Shop → Combat (on continue), Combat → Death (when all players dead), Death → Lab (after delay/click), Lab → Combat (new run). Use useReducer for state management with actions like TRANSITION_TO_SHOP, TRANSITION_TO_DEATH, etc. Include validation to prevent invalid transitions.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for phase transition logic, integration tests for automatic transitions, verify all valid phase combinations work correctly

subtasks.title: Design the Phase State Model
subtasks.description: Define the complete phase state structure including all possible phases, their properties, and the data model that will be managed throughout the application lifecycle.
subtasks.details: Create TypeScript interfaces/types for: phase enumeration (e.g., SETUP, ACTIVE, PAUSED, COMPLETED), phase state object with properties like currentPhase, previousPhase, phaseData, timestamps, and metadata. Define the shape of data that each phase will contain and any phase-specific configurations or settings.

subtasks.title: Create the React Context Provider
subtasks.description: Implement the React Context provider component that will wrap the application and provide phase state and dispatch functions to child components.
subtasks.details: Create PhaseContext using React.createContext, implement PhaseProvider component that initializes the phase state, provides context value with state and dispatch, and handles context consumer error boundaries. Include proper TypeScript typing for context value and ensure the provider can be easily integrated into the app component tree.

subtasks.title: Implement Transition Logic for Each Phase
subtasks.description: Create the core transition logic that handles moving between different phases, including the business rules and conditions for each transition.
subtasks.details: Implement transition functions for each phase change (e.g., setupToActive, activeTopaused, pausedToActive, activeToCompleted). Define transition conditions, side effects, and data transformations that occur during each phase change. Create helper functions to determine valid next phases from current phase and handle any cleanup or initialization required during transitions.

subtasks.title: Add Validation for Transitions
subtasks.description: Implement comprehensive validation logic to ensure phase transitions are valid and prevent invalid state changes.
subtasks.details: Create validation functions that check: if a transition from current phase to target phase is allowed, if required data/conditions are met before transition, if user permissions allow the transition, and if system state supports the transition. Implement error handling for invalid transitions with descriptive error messages and logging.

subtasks.title: Integrate useReducer with Actions
subtasks.description: Implement the useReducer hook with action creators and reducer function to manage phase state updates in a predictable way.
subtasks.details: Create action types and action creators for all phase operations (TRANSITION_PHASE, UPDATE_PHASE_DATA, RESET_PHASE, etc.). Implement the phase reducer function that handles each action type, applies validation, executes transitions, and returns new state. Integrate the reducer with the context provider and ensure all state updates go through the reducer pattern.

subtasks.title: Write Unit and Integration Tests
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive test suites covering all aspects of the phase management system including unit tests for individual functions and integration tests for the complete system.
subtasks.details: Write unit tests for: phase state model validation, individual transition functions, validation logic, reducer actions and state updates. Create integration tests for: context provider functionality, complete phase transition flows, error handling scenarios, and edge cases. Include tests for React component integration, mock scenarios, and performance testing for state updates.

tasks.title: Create Phase Tracker UI Component
tasks.description: Build a persistent phase tracker component that displays on the left side of the screen, showing current phase and overall game loop progress.
tasks.details: Create PhaseTracker component using Tailwind CSS with fixed positioning on left side. Display current phase with visual indicators (icons, colors). Show game loop progression with visual breadcrumbs or progress bar. Use React context to subscribe to phase changes. Style with consistent design: bg-gray-800 text-white p-4 fixed left-0 top-0 h-full w-64. Include phase icons and transition animations.
tasks.testStrategy: Visual regression tests, verify tracker updates correctly on phase changes, test responsive design on different screen sizes

tasks.title: Refactor Combat System into Separate Module
tasks.description: Extract existing combat simulator logic into a dedicated Combat component and module, maintaining current functionality while preparing for phase integration.
tasks.details: Create src/components/Combat.tsx and src/utils/combatLogic.ts. Move combat state management, enemy generation, and battle logic into separate files. Implement Combat component that integrates with phase system - automatically transitions to Shop when all enemies defeated. Keep Reset button for development that only resets current combat. Export combat utilities: generateEnemies(), processCombatRound(), checkVictoryCondition(). Use TypeScript interfaces for all combat entities.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for combat logic functions, integration tests for phase transitions, verify Reset button only affects current combat

tasks.title: Implement Shop Phase Component
tasks.description: Create Shop screen component with placeholder upgrades for characters and Lab, including purchase simulation and continue functionality.
tasks.details: Create src/components/Shop.tsx with placeholder upgrade items. Display upgrades in grid layout using Tailwind: grid grid-cols-2 gap-4. Include character upgrades (health boost, damage boost) and Lab upgrades (facility improvements). Implement mock purchase logic - no real currency yet, just simulate buying. Add Continue button that triggers transition to next Combat phase with increased difficulty. Style with consistent UI: bg-gray-100 p-6 rounded-lg shadow-md for upgrade cards.
tasks.testStrategy: Component tests for Shop rendering, test purchase simulation, verify Continue button triggers correct phase transition

subtasks.title: Implement Gold/Income System
subtasks.description: Create the core economic system for the shop phase including gold tracking, income calculation, and currency management
subtasks.details: Develop gold state management, income calculation based on previous battle performance, gold display components, and currency validation logic. Include methods for adding/subtracting gold and persisting gold state across phases.

subtasks.title: Build Shop UI Layout and Item Display
subtasks.description: Create the visual shop interface with item grid, categories, and responsive layout
subtasks.details: Design and implement shop container, item grid layout, item cards with images/descriptions/prices, category filters, and responsive design. Include hover effects and visual feedback for interactive elements.

subtasks.title: Implement Purchase Logic and Validation
subtasks.description: Create the core purchase mechanics including item selection, price validation, and transaction processing
subtasks.details: Develop purchase validation (sufficient gold, item availability), transaction processing, purchase confirmation dialogs, error handling for failed purchases, and update gold balance after successful purchases.

subtasks.title: Create Inventory Management System
subtasks.description: Implement inventory storage, item tracking, and inventory UI components
subtasks.details: Build inventory data structure, purchased items storage, inventory display panel, item stacking logic for consumables, and inventory capacity management. Include visual indicators for inventory status.

subtasks.title: Implement Drag-and-Drop for Item Application
subtasks.description: Create drag-and-drop functionality to apply items from inventory to character cards
subtasks.details: Implement draggable inventory items, drop zones on character cards, drag preview components, item application logic, visual feedback during drag operations, and validation for item-character compatibility.

subtasks.title: Handle Shop Phase Transition and Continue Logic
subtasks.description: Implement phase transition mechanics and continue button functionality to exit shop phase
subtasks.details: Create continue button with proper state validation, save shop state before transition, implement phase transition logic to next game phase, handle cleanup of shop-specific UI elements, and ensure proper state persistence.

tasks.title: Create Death Phase Component
tasks.description: Implement Death screen that displays when all player characters die, with automatic transition to Lab phase after delay or user interaction.
tasks.details: Create src/components/Death.tsx with game over messaging and visual feedback. Display static image or animated death screen with message 'Your team has fallen...' Use setTimeout for automatic transition to Lab after 3 seconds, or immediate transition on button click. Style with dark theme: bg-red-900 text-white min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center. Include restart option and run statistics display.
tasks.testStrategy: Component tests for Death screen rendering, test automatic transition timing, verify manual transition button works

tasks.title: Create Lab Phase Placeholder Component
tasks.description: Build placeholder Lab screen component with future evolution system messaging and new run initialization.
tasks.details: Create src/components/Lab.tsx with placeholder content. Display message: 'Lab/Evolution phase coming soon.' with futuristic styling. Include 'Start New Run' button that resets upgrades, generates new team, and transitions to Combat phase. Style with sci-fi theme: bg-blue-900 text-cyan-300 with glowing effects. Prepare component structure for future evolution mechanics with placeholder sections for breeding, genetic engineering, etc.
tasks.testStrategy: Component tests for Lab rendering, verify new run button resets game state correctly, test transition to Combat phase

tasks.title: Create Main App Layout and Routing System
tasks.description: Implement main application layout that renders appropriate phase components based on current phase state, with persistent phase tracker.
tasks.details: Refactor main.tsx to focus on high-level app structure. Create layout with phase tracker on left and main content area on right. Implement phase routing: switch statement or component mapping to render Combat, Shop, Death, or Lab based on current phase. Use CSS Grid or Flexbox: grid-template-columns: 256px 1fr. Ensure overlay UI elements can be rendered above phase screens. Structure: <PhaseProvider><Layout><PhaseTracker /><MainContent /></Layout></PhaseProvider>
tasks.testStrategy: Integration tests for phase routing, verify layout responsiveness, test overlay rendering capabilities

tasks.title: Create Types and Interfaces Module
tasks.description: Extract all TypeScript types and interfaces into dedicated types module for better code organization and reusability.
tasks.details: Create src/types/index.ts with all game-related interfaces: Character, Enemy, Phase, GameState, ShopItem, LabUpgrade, CombatResult, etc. Define union types for phases: type Phase = 'combat' | 'shop' | 'death' | 'lab'. Include utility types for state management and component props. Export all types from single index file. Use strict TypeScript configuration with proper type definitions for all game entities and state structures.
tasks.testStrategy: TypeScript compilation tests, verify all components use proper types, test type safety across modules

tasks.title: Create Utility Functions Module
tasks.description: Extract combat logic, enemy generation, and other utility functions into dedicated utils module for better code organization.
tasks.details: Create src/utils/index.ts with combat utilities: calculateDamage(), generateEnemyWave(), processInitiative(), checkGameOver(). Include helper functions for phase transitions, difficulty scaling, and game state management. Implement pure functions with no side effects for easy testing. Export functions: { combatUtils, gameUtils, mathUtils }. Use functional programming patterns where appropriate and include JSDoc comments for all functions.
tasks.testStrategy: Comprehensive unit tests for all utility functions, test edge cases and error handling, verify pure function behavior

tasks.title: Implement Extensible Architecture Foundation
tasks.description: Design and implement extensible architecture patterns to support future features like evolution mechanics, new enemy types, and advanced combat systems.
tasks.details: Implement plugin-like architecture for abilities, upgrades, and game mechanics. Create base classes/interfaces for extensibility: BaseAbility, BaseUpgrade, BaseEnemy. Use composition over inheritance patterns. Implement event system for game actions using custom hooks or context. Create configuration objects for easy feature toggling. Structure code with clear separation of concerns: data layer, business logic, UI components. Include comprehensive documentation and examples for extending the system.
tasks.testStrategy: Architecture tests for extensibility patterns, verify new features can be added without breaking existing code, test plugin system

subtasks.title: Design base classes and interfaces for effect system
subtasks.description: Create abstract base classes and interfaces that define the contract for all item effects, including IEffect interface with methods for apply(), getTargetingMechanics(), getUIElements(), and base Effect class with common properties like id, name, description, and validation logic.
subtasks.details: Define TypeScript interfaces and abstract classes that establish the foundation for the plugin architecture. Include methods for effect application, targeting validation, UI state management, and configuration handling.

subtasks.title: Implement plugin architecture for effect registration
subtasks.description: Create an EffectRegistry system that allows effects to be dynamically registered and retrieved, with factory patterns for effect instantiation and dependency injection for shared services like UI state management.
subtasks.details: Build a centralized registry that manages effect lifecycle, handles effect discovery, and provides a clean API for registering new effects without modifying core system code.

subtasks.title: Create global event system and UI state management
subtasks.description: Implement a global event bus and state management system for UI elements like popups and highlights that can be accessed across UnitCard, shop, and combat screens. Include helper functions for showGeneticPopup, setHealedUnitId, and setFlashUnitId.
subtasks.details: Design a reactive state management system that allows effects to trigger UI changes globally without tight coupling. Create exported helper functions that effects can use to manage UI state consistently.

subtasks.title: Refactor existing effects and implement configuration system
subtasks.description: Migrate genetic potential effect to use the new architecture with global state for popup display, simplify ShopScreen item handling to single-line team state updates, and create configuration objects for effect properties including targeting mechanics and UI behavior.
subtasks.details: Convert existing effects to the new plugin system, ensuring genetic potential effect demonstrates the global popup functionality. Streamline shop interactions and embed effect-specific logic within configuration objects.

subtasks.title: Separate concerns and write extensibility documentation
subtasks.description: Restructure code to separate effect logic from UI handling and business logic, then create comprehensive documentation covering how to create new effects, register them with the system, and utilize the available UI helpers and targeting mechanics.
subtasks.details: Ensure clean separation between effect implementation, UI management, and core game logic. Provide detailed guides, code examples, and API documentation for developers adding new effects to the system.

tasks.title: Implement Efficient State Management with Immer
tasks.description: Integrate Immer library for efficient immutable state updates to handle complex game state changes without performance issues.
tasks.details: Install Immer: npm install immer @types/immer. Create state management hooks using Immer's produce function for immutable updates. Implement useImmerReducer for complex state transitions. Example: const [gameState, updateGameState] = useImmerReducer(gameReducer, initialState). Use Immer for character updates, combat state changes, and shop transactions. Create helper functions: updateCharacterStats(), processShopPurchase(), advanceGamePhase(). Ensure all state updates are immutable and efficient.
tasks.testStrategy: Performance tests comparing Immer vs deep cloning, verify state immutability, test complex state update scenarios

tasks.title: Polish UI and Implement Consistent Design System
tasks.description: Create consistent UI design system using Tailwind CSS, implement responsive design, and ensure clean modern interface across all phases.
tasks.details: Create design system with consistent color palette, typography, and spacing using Tailwind CSS custom configuration. Implement responsive design for mobile and desktop. Create reusable UI components: Button, Card, Modal, ProgressBar. Use consistent styling patterns: primary colors (blue-600, blue-700), secondary (gray-600), success (green-600), danger (red-600). Implement smooth transitions between phases with CSS animations. Create loading states and error handling UI. Ensure accessibility with proper ARIA labels and keyboard navigation.
tasks.testStrategy: Visual regression tests, accessibility testing with screen readers, responsive design testing across devices, user experience testing

tasks.title: Implement Enemy Level Scaling System
tasks.description: Create a comprehensive enemy scaling system that generates progressively stronger enemies with increased experience rewards as players advance through missions, with unique enemy sets and scaling logic per world.
tasks.details: Create src/utils/enemyScaling.ts with world-specific enemy generation functions. Implement base enemy types with scaling formulas: health = baseHealth * (1 + level * 0.2), damage = baseDamage * (1 + level * 0.15), experience = baseExp * (1 + level * 0.3). Design world system with unique enemy pools: World1 (basic creatures), World2 (elemental beings), World3 (mechanical units). Create EnemyScalingConfig interface with properties: worldId, baseEnemies[], scalingMultipliers, bossThreshold. Implement generateScaledEnemies(worldId, missionLevel) function that selects appropriate enemies and applies scaling. Add boss generation logic: when missionLevel % 5 === 0, spawn boss with 3x health/damage multipliers. Create enemy progression system that tracks player advancement and adjusts difficulty curves. Include enemy variant system where higher levels unlock elite versions with special abilities. Implement world transition logic that unlocks new worlds based on boss defeats. Use composition pattern for enemy abilities and traits to support extensibility.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for scaling formulas with various level inputs, verify world-specific enemy generation produces correct types, test boss spawning at appropriate intervals, validate experience scaling calculations, integration tests for enemy progression through multiple missions, test world transition triggers, verify elite enemy variants appear at correct levels
